- The windscreen sealant can be cut using a piano wire or vibrating knife; both methods are described below.

- To cut using a piano wire, proceed as described below.

1. Cut a length of wire of about 50 cm then, using pliers, introduce one end (1a) of the wire through bead of sealant (1b) securing windscreen (1c).

2. Fasten one end (1a) of the wire to special retaining tool (2a) located inside the vehicle.

Fasten one end (2b) of the wire to traction handle (2c) located outside the vehicle.

3. The mechanic inside the vehicle should keep the end of tool (2a) on sealant bead (3) about 30 cm from the point where the wire passes through.

The other mechanic, outside the vehicle, should pull handle (2c), following the surround of the windscreen and cut sealant bead (3).

Position a spatula (2d) against tool (2a) to protect the dashboard trim.

Repeat the operation in sections of about 30 cm until bead of sealant (3) is completely cut.

- To cut using a vibrating knife, proceed as described below.

1. Use vibrating knife (1a) and blade (1b) and working from the outside of the vehicle, cut the sealant bead along inner side (1c) of the windscreen .

2. Fit blade (2a) and, working from inside the vehicle, cut the sealant strip along all other sides (2b) of the windscreen.
1. After cutting round the entire sealant strip, apply suction pads to the windscreen and then, with the assistance of a second mechanic, remove the windscreen and rest it on a support stand.

1. Using suitable equipment, cut and level the bead of sealant in the windscreen housing leaving a thickness of between 0.25 and 1 mm, taking care not to scratch the paintwork. The thickness of the sealant remaining in the housing will act as a support for the new bonding.

2. Clean the windscreen seat thoroughly using compressed air and degrease carefully with heptane. When bonding, 60 minutes after the bead of sealant has been cut and levelled, the surface of the actual sealant must be treated using the special activating product and it is necessary to wait for 15 minutes before fitting the windscreen.

- New window preparation.

1. Degrease screen-printed perimeter (1a) of the new windscreen using heptane. Also degrease the seat to which upper seal (1b) is bonded.

2. Apply glass adhesion promoter (primer) (2b) to screen-printed perimeter using wick (2a) supplied in the kit.

Wait for about 15 minutes before continuing with the next operation to allow the adhesion promoter (primer) thinner to evaporate.

3. Position new seal (1b) in its seat on the upper side of the windscreen, ensuring adhesive part (3a) bonds to the windscreen as shown in the figure.

- Preparing a removed window.

1. A removed window is reusable only if it did not suffer damage during removal. In particular, seal (1a) present along the side edges must be intact.

2. Using suitable equipment cut and level the bead of sealant on the windscreen so that it is as thin as possible. The remaining sealant does not have to be completely removed; take care not to damage the black screen-printing on the glass perimeter.

3. Clean the perimeter of the screen-printed area of the windscreen thoroughly with compressed air and degrease it using heptane.

Also degrease the seat to which upper seal (1b) is bonded.

Check that the glass is not damaged.

4. Position new seal (1b) in its seat on the upper side of the windscreen, ensuring adhesive part (4a) bonds to the windscreen as shown in the figure.

5. When bonding, 60 minutes after the bead of sealant has been cut and levelled, the surface of the actual sealant must be treated using the special activating product and it is necessary to wait for 15 minutes before fitting the windscreen.
